notes: Scripted encounters: named people who come on a set day with set goods and words, some of them again and again until you serve them. `need`: 'auto' is the need your own stock serves most. `rate`: what a buyer pays over worth, or the fraction of worth a seller asks for the lot. `after`: another beat that must be done first. `again`: they keep coming each day until the deal is done. `gift`: what they leave you after the deal. `thanks`: what they say after it.

beats.name: Pim
beats.line: Tug came in heavy and the dock store won't take the overflow. Take it off my hands before the shift bell.

beats.name: Wren
beats.line: Foundry paid out today. I'll pay over for anything that doesn't taste of slag.
beats.thanks: Worth the walk. I'll tell the shift where the good counter is.

beats.name: Mara
beats.line: The recycler on our bunk row is rationing again. Six credits is all I have left.
beats.thanks: Fair price, and no sneer about it. I won't forget a counter like that.

beats.name: Skip
beats.line: Fell off a tug. Not that it was ever on one. Dream tabs for the bunks, crank for the foundry, and the flame is the real thing. Fire's worth three times what it burns.

beats.name: Corvin
beats.line: The deck inspector walks through at third bell. I need real parts on the books, and I pay for the paperwork.
beats.thanks: Receipts in order. You're on my list of reliable stalls.

beats.name: Pim
beats.line: You took the overflow without haggling. Here's the next run's ore at a regular's price.

beats.name: Mara
beats.line: My mother's locket. It's the only thing worth anything I own, and you were fair to me. It should be somewhere kind.
